result.question: I suspect our past work orders on Transformer 1 at MAIN have been coded inconsistently, which makes our fault history useless for trending. Pull all work orders on Transformer 1, open and closed, and show me each one's number, description, status and failure code. Then read our failure code catalog and map each code to the closest transformer fault class or failure mode: partial discharge, low-energy arcing, high-energy arcing, oil overheating, core/winding thermal, tap changer wear, moisture ingress, cellulose ageing or oil dielectric degradation. Flag every work order whose code doesn't match its description, and every one that has no code at all, and suggest the correct code for each. Also run a fault classification on the latest oil sample and tell me whether any open work order is coded for a different fault than the gases currently indicate. Only propose recodes, and don't change anything yourself unless the work order is still open and the description clearly names the fault. In that case, update its failure code and list what you changed. If the catalog has no code that fits a fault class, say so and recommend a new code rather than forcing a poor match.
result.answer:
## Work orders on Transformer 1 (MAIN)

| WO | Description | Status | Failure code |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection - Transformer 1 on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | WAPPR (open) | **none** |
| 1000052 | Transformer 1 oil sample retest and insulation check - DGA thermal fault (Rogers 1-0-2, T3 hot metal) | WAPPR (open) | FC006 |

## Catalog mapping (transformer fault classes → FCC codes)

The FCC catalog is symptom-oriented, not transformer-specific. Best available mappings:

| Fault class | Closest FCC code |
|---|---|
| Partial discharge | none — no code fits |
| Low-energy arcing / high-energy arcing | none — no code fits |
| Oil overheating / core-winding thermal | FC006 (overheating / high temperature) — partial fit |
| Tap changer wear | none — no code fits |
| Moisture ingress | FC004 (fluid leak) — poor fit |
| Cellulose ageing | FC006 — very poor fit |
| Oil dielectric degradation | FC008 (gauge) — no; none fits |

## Issues flagged

1. **WO 1000051 — no failure code.** Description clearly names the fault (OLTC contact wear/coking). The catalog has **no tap-changer code**; do not force FC006 ("overheating") onto it. Recommend a new code, e.g. **FC011 – tap changer contact wear/coking**.
2. **WO 1000052 — code FC006.** Description names a DGA thermal fault (Rogers 1-0-2, T3 hot metal). FC006 ("overheating/high temperature") is a reasonable match for a thermal fault, so the code is **consistent** with the description — not flagged as mismatched.

## DGA fault classification (latest sample, 2024-01-19)

Note: the interpretive DGA tool was unavailable (LLM error), so this classification is computed directly from the latest oil sample values:

- H2 = 2850 ppm, CH4 = 7400, C2H6 = 5470, C2H4 = 16650, C2H2 = 7
- Ratios: CH4/H2 = 7400/2850 ≈ 2.6 (>1 → code 1); C2H6/CH4 = 5470/7400 ≈ 0.74 (<1 → code 0); C2H4/C2H6 = 16650/5470 ≈ 3.05 (>1 → code 2)
- Rogers code **1-0-2 → T3 fault: thermal fault in the range 700 °C – hot metal contact**

Current gas signature points to **high-temperature thermal fault / hot metal contact** — consistent with the OLTC contact-wear/coking suspicion in WO 1000051 and the thermal framing in WO 1000052.

## Open WO coded for a different fault than gases indicate?

- **WO 1000052** (FC006, thermal): matches the current T3 thermal signature. Not a mismatch.
- **WO 1000051** (no code): the gas signature (hot metal contact, T3) is consistent with the OLTC contact wear/coking named in its description. It is uncoded rather than mis-coded — which is exactly the gap that breaks trending.

## Recode proposals (no changes made)

- **WO 1000051**: needs a code. It's open and the description clearly names the fault, but **the catalog has no suitable code**, so I recommend creating **a new failure code (e.g. FC011: tap changer contact wear/coking)** rather than forcing FC006. I have not assigned any code since no existing one fits.
- **WO 1000052**: FC006 matches the description; no change proposed.

No work orders were updated, since the only recodable open WO (1000051) has no matching catalog code.
